overview: Baldwin IV was king of Jerusalem while living with leprosy and facing the military rise of Saladin. His reign combined personal illness, factional politics, and moments of striking battlefield success.
Baldwin’s legacy is powerful because his personal courage became intertwined with the kingdom’s last years before Hattin.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Baldwin IV was king of Jerusalem while living with leprosy and facing the military rise of Saladin. His reign combined personal illness, factional politics, and moments of striking battlefield success.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Baldwin was son of Amalric I and was educated at court by William of Tyre, who later described the discovery of his illness.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Baldwin IV of Jerusalem is remembered as one of the most poignant and admired figures of the crusader east: the "leper king" whose courage and resolve defied a disease that was slowly destroying him. The sources, above all William of Tyre, who had been his tutor, present a young ruler of remarkable intelligence, dignity, and bravery, who insisted on leading his kingdom and even his armies despite the progressive ravages of leprosy.

His tutor's account is affectionate and admiring, recording how the boy's illness was first noticed and how the young king refused to be reduced by it — most strikingly in his personal leadership at the victory of Montgisard against Saladin while still in his teens. The sources convey a ruler of unusual strength of will, holding a fracturing kingdom together by sheer determination as his body failed.

Because the fullest portrait comes from a devoted teacher, the admiration is heartfelt and partisan, but the core is well grounded in the documented record of his reign. He is remembered as a tragic and heroic figure — clear-minded, courageous, and dutiful — whose personal valour against both Saladin and his own disease made him one of the most sympathetic rulers of the crusading age.

contentSections.title: As king under the shadow of leprosy
paragraphs: Baldwin became king as a minor and ruled amid noble rivalries over succession and regency. He defeated Saladin at Montgisard in 1177, but his worsening illness made the kingdom’s future increasingly unstable.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Baldwin died in 1185, leaving a contested succession that soon passed through Baldwin V, Sibylla, and Guy of Lusignan.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Baldwin’s legacy is powerful because his personal courage became intertwined with the kingdom’s last years before Hattin.
